Subject: Onprem hotpatch phased commit playbook & canary window

Folks — attaching the first draft of the phased-commit playbook for the on-prem/private fleet hotpatch we discussed. High level: we want to ship a critical JVM patch that fixes a memory edge case; changes are tiny but impact on persistent KV shards makes us treat this like a hotpatch.

Planned approach (short):
- Phased commits by pod group (see canary CSV) with a quick health probe (10m observation) after each pod slice.
- Canary set: 3 pods in staging -> 5 pods in customer-sim -> 10 pods in canary-1 (Acme region)
- Rollback triggers: >1% error-rate delta sustained 5m OR tail-latency 95th increases >50ms sustained 5m. Detailed criteria in rollback_criteria_v2.pdf.
- Escalation path: SRE (Neha) -> Platform Lead (Soojin) -> Ops point (Acme).

Requested from Acme: confirm maintenance window preference (we proposed UTC 02:00-06:00 Fri) and provide contact for emergency network interventions.

Attachments: onprem_canary_schedule_v1.csv, rollback_criteria_v2.pdf, hotpatch_runbook_draft.md

Next actions (mine): merge any critical edits by EOD today, lock canary schedule by 17:00 PT, standup shiproom on Friday morning.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onprem hotpatch phased commit playbook & canary window

Thanks Marcus — quick clarifications before I sign off on the runbook: 
1) Health probes: are we running the probe as synthetic traffic hitting the same KV hotkeys we saw in the incident, or simple API-level pings? The probe type changes noise characteristics.
2) Isolation plan: if canary pod set signals, do we quarantine traffic at load-balancer level (route to standby pool) or by evicting pods and letting autoscaler refill? Which is faster to mitigate customer impact?

I agree with the rollback thresholds but would like a secondary safety net: an automated prefix-cache invalidation as part of rollout steps to avoid stale-state exposure. If Acme's environment has sticky networking, that needs to be tested in the first canary tranche.

I'll be on the shiproom if we lock window.

-Neha
SRE, Redwood Inference

Quick follow-up with the test plan and gating matrix (excerpt below). I've added the cache invalidation step Neha requested as an automated job after each successful tranche. Full matrix in the runbook attachment.

Gating matrix (summary):
- Tranche 1 (staging, 3 pods): pass = 0 new errors, cpu/mem within baseline +/-5%, 95p latency delta < 20ms over baseline (10m steady).
- Tranche 2 (customer-sim, 5 pods): pass = error delta < 0.2%, tail-latency <= baseline +30ms, KV-consistency probes OK.
- Tranche 3 (canary-1 Acme, 10 pods): pass = error delta < 0.5%, tail-latency <= baseline +50ms, no consumer-side timeouts.

Rollback automation: if any tranche fails, the orchestrator will stop commits and attempt a priority revert to previous image within the same minute; manual escalation if revert does not stabilize within 10 minutes. Revert steps are idempotent and documented in rollback_criteria_v2.pdf.

I also added a preflight checklist for network teams: BGP session health, MTU check (we saw a flaky MTU in staging last month), and firewall rule drift verification. Acme, please confirm these checks are green on your side before window.

- Soojin
Platform Lead, Redwood Inference

Folks — I reviewed the playbook and the gating criteria. Given the customer risk and compliance needs I approve the proposed phased approach with the following conditions: 
1) All preflight checks (BGP, MTU, firewall drift) must be signed off by Acme and posted in the Drive link before start.
2) Shiproom must include a compliance observer to capture change artifacts for the SOC2 evidence bundle. Neha, can your team own evidence capture (timestamps, logs, audit IDs)?
3) If network-level mitigation is required (BGP reset, PB rules changes) we escalate to Acme's Victor — do not attempt network-level interventions without Acme permission.

Once those conditions are satisfied, proceed with the adjusted window (Fri 03:00-07:00 UTC). Please confirm readiness by 16:00 PT today.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
